subject: math
title: Add and Subtract Within 1000
seo_title: Grade 3 Addition and Subtraction Within 1000 Worksheets: 3-Digit Regrouping and Word Problems
domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standard_text: Fluently add and subtract within 1000 using strategies and algorithms based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 worksheets for adding and subtracting 3-digit numbers: regrouping, subtracting across zeros, missing numbers, estimating to check and word problems. 100 practice questions with step-by-step answers.
key_big: Line up the places. Start with the ones. Regroup when you need to.
key_sub: Adding: 10 ones make 1 ten, 10 tens make 1 hundred. Subtracting: if the top digit is smaller, take 1 from the next place to the left. Check by adding back.
body_html:
Line up the places

Every 3-digit number has hundreds, tens and ones. Write the numbers in columns so ones are under ones, tens under tens and hundreds under hundreds. Then work from the ones to the left.

Add by place value

You can also break the numbers apart and add each place.

Place347 + 285Sum
Hundreds300 + 200500
Tens40 + 80120
Ones7 + 512
Total500 + 120 + 12632

Subtract with regrouping

If the top digit is smaller, regroup: take 1 from the next place to the left and make 10 in this place.

Subtract across zeros

What is 500 − 263?

The tens place is 0, so regroup 1 hundred as 10 tens first. Then regroup 1 ten as 10 ones. Now it is 4 hundreds, 9 tens, 10 ones. Ones: 10 − 3 = 7. Tens: 9 − 6 = 3. Hundreds: 4 − 2 = 2.

Answer: 237

Check your answer

Addition and subtraction undo each other. After subtracting, add your answer to the number you took away. You should get the number you started with: 365 + 258 = 623. You can also estimate: 623 − 258 is about 600 − 300 = 300, so 365 makes sense.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting the regrouped 1 (347 + 285 = 522)Write the small 1 above the next column and add it
Taking the smaller digit from the bigger one (623 − 258 = 435)Always take the bottom digit from the top digit. Regroup when the top is smaller
Regrouping but not crossing out (623 − 258 = 475)When you take 1 ten, the tens digit gets 1 smaller
Lining up the numbers on the leftLine up the ones on the right

faq.q: How do you add 3-digit numbers with regrouping?
faq.a: Line up the ones, tens and hundreds. Add the ones first. If the sum is 10 or more, write the ones digit and regroup 1 ten to the tens column. Do the same for the tens, then add the hundreds.

faq.q: How do you subtract across zeros, like 500 − 263?
faq.a: There are no tens to regroup, so first regroup 1 hundred as 10 tens. Then regroup 1 ten as 10 ones. Now you have 4 hundreds, 9 tens and 10 ones, and you can subtract each place: 237.

faq.q: How can my child check a subtraction answer?
faq.a: Add the answer to the number that was subtracted. If you get the starting number, the answer is right. For 623 − 258 = 365, check 365 + 258 = 623.
It is the Common Core standard for Grade 3: fluently add and subtract within 1000 using place value strategies, properties of operations and the link between addition and subtraction.
